decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%.

changes.quote: Labor market conditions have improved further; the unemployment rate has declined notably in recent months but remains elevated.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledges that job markets are getting better and unemployment has dropped recently, though it still considers the rate too high.

changes.quote: Strains in global financial markets have eased, though they continue to pose significant downside risks to the economic outlook.
changes.explanation: While international financial stress has decreased, the Fed still sees overseas risks that could hurt the domestic economy.

changes.quote: Inflation has been subdued in recent months, although prices of crude oil and gasoline have increased lately.
changes.explanation: General inflation has remained calm, but rising energy and gas prices are starting to add cost pressures.

tone_quotes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that the economy has been expanding moderately.

To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee expects to maintain a highly accommodative stance for monetary policy.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.36% APR costs about $51.50 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.14% and moved +10 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.9% would rise by about $17.24 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 8.3%, and employers added an average of 273k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year (February 2012); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.14% on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to hold interest rates at exceptionally low levels at least through late 2014. Officials will continue monitoring economic data and adjust their securities holdings as appropriate to promote a stronger economic recovery.

citations.detail: In particular, the Committee decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that economic conditions--including low rates of resource utilization and a subdued outlook for inflation over the medium run--are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate at least through late 2014.

llm_decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep its benchmark interest rate at zero to 1/4 percent and maintain its timeline for exceptionally low rates at least through late 2014.
